newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany faces moderate growth in 1997-bank group.
newsitem.headline: Germany faces moderate growth in 1997-bank group.

text.p: The German economy is likely to show moderate growth during 1997 as an underlying uptrend is tempered by weak consumer demand and stubbornly high unemployment, the BdB German Banking Asociation said Thursday.

In its latest economic report, the BdB predicted that German growth would average two to 2.5 percent over the year, driven mainly by spending on equipment, as building investments would likely drop again.
The group, which represents commercial banks, blamed the modest outlook on structural problems in Germany, saying the state's 51 percent share of gross domestic product (GDP) was too high.
